content.title: About
content.content: Pesto sauce is a classic Italian condiment made from fresh basil, olive oil, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, and garlic. It has a bright aroma, rich flavor, and is used as a pasta dressing, spread on bread, or an accompaniment to meat and fish dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name pesto comes from the Italian verb “pestare,” meaning “to crush” in a mortar.
Traditional Genoese pesto is prepared in a marble mortar, which helps preserve the basil’s aroma.
Pine nuts in the original recipe can be substituted with walnuts or almonds without major flavor loss.
In the United States, pesto is often made with added spinach or parsley to reduce cost.
There are many pesto variations: arugula, sun‑dried tomato, pecan, and even avocado pesto.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Basil provides polyphenols and vitamin K, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil supplies monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: Basil and garlic deliver vitamins A and C, important for immunity and vision.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Parmesan adds calcium and phosphorus, essential for strong bones.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Pine nuts and basil contribute modest amounts of fiber that aid digestion.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Pine nuts can trigger allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Olive oil and nuts make the sauce calorie‑rich; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Parmesan adds sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Microbial risk
items.content: Fresh herbs can carry bacteria; keep the sauce refrigerated and consume within a week.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pesto pairs wonderfully with pasta, rice, couscous, as a marinade for chicken, fish or vegetables, and as a spread on bread, crackers, or sandwiches. It can be stirred into soups or used as a pizza sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pesto in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5–7 days. For longer keeping, freeze in small portions; after thawing, stir as the oil may separate.
